newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Chubb shares drop 25 pct on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Chubb shares drop 25 pct on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in South African engineering group Chubb Holdings Ltd on Friday shed 25 percent of their value after the group warned its year profits are to fall.

Chubb stock was marked down 600 cents to a new year low of 18.00 rand on the news, but trade was light with only 500 shares trading hands by 0950 GMT. "Obviously, this is very bad news for the stock," one dealer said.
Analysts said the news had caught the market by surprise. "It was unexpected and that explains the sharpness of the drop," one analyst said.
Chubb said first half profits were expected to be "substantially" below year-ago levels and no improvement was expected in the second half.
"As a consequence, the profits for the full year are expected to be below those of last year," the company said.
Chubb posted attributable income of 18.37 million rand in the year ended March 31, 1996, from 17.19 million in the previous period.

Chubb blamed the profit dive on an investment and reorganisation programme had proceeded more slowly than anticipated. The company had also experienced erosion in margins and a sharp increase in overheads, in part due to start-up costs.
Analysts said the firm may also be being hit by an increase in competition at its security division as rivals seek to capitalise on the profit opportunities afforded by South Africa's crime wave.
